# Public library and museum (`public_library_museum`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/institutions.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Institutions, law & governance (`institutions`)
- Deps: helped by library_catalogue, codex_book, printing_press, charitable_endowment_waqf
- Core idea: A collection of books, specimens, instruments and works of art kept at public or endowed expense and open to any reader without fee. One copy then serves hundreds, a craftsman or student with no money can reach the best knowledge, and objects are preserved and compared instead of scattered at an owner's death. It needs a permanent income, a keeper, a catalogue, fixed opening hours, a reading room, and rules against theft and fire. Lending is optional; access is the point.
- Pitfalls:
  - Calling Alexandria or Ashurbanipal's library public: both served a court and its scholars
  - No catalogue and no keeper means the books cannot be found and soon vanish
  - A single great collection is one fire away from loss; copies distributed among many libraries are what preserve texts
  - Repeating that Caesar or the Arabs destroyed the Library of Alexandria in one blaze: it declined over centuries of neglect, war and lost funding
- History: mesopotamia: 7th c. BC – Ashurbanipal's palace library at Nineveh, some 30,000 tablets and fragments, systematically collected and labelled; egypt: c. 280 BC – royal Library of Alexandria attached to the Museum; rome: 39 BC – Asinius Pollio opens Rome's first public library; by the 4th c. the city lists 28; china: 26 BC – the Han imperial library is collated and catalogued; great private libraries such as the Tianyi Ge (1561) admitted few; public libraries from the 1900s; india: 5th–12th c. – the monastic libraries of Nalanda, for residents and visiting monks; islamic: 1005 – the Dar al-Ilm in Cairo, open to all with free ink and paper (al-Maqrizi); endowed mosque and madrasa libraries with lending; europe: 1444 – library of San Marco, Florence, open to scholars; 1602 Bodleian; 1683 Ashmolean Museum, Oxford, open to paying public; 1759 British Museum opens free; 1793 Louvre; 1850 British Public Libraries Act; americas: 1731 – Franklin's subscription Library Company; 1833 Peterborough, New Hampshire, tax-supported; 1854 Boston Public Library opens
- Read:
  - Lionel Casson, Libraries in the Ancient World (2001)
  - Matthew Battles, Library: An Unquiet History (2003)
